item.title: China Open Source Daily — 2026-11-06
item.description: The public consultation on MOFCOM and MOST Announcement No. 48 closes on 2026-11-15, and the draft's answer to the question Chinese open-weight labs have been waiting for turns out to be a legal construction rather than an exemption. Annex 1 excludes technologies that have already entered the public domain 'through open source, academic publication or other means' — but the same instrument that creates the carve-out has already decided that open-sourcing is itself a technology export subject to pre-export registration. The interim registration has been live since 2026-10-16, and legal analysis published by Fangda on 2026-10-20 reads its third trigger — a change in the owner or actual controller of domestic technology to an overseas entity — as a deemed-export rule that acts without any movement of technology across a border, and identifies automatic licensing for restricted AI technologies in five named scenarios including open sourcing, building one's own overseas compute centre, overseas tape-out, joint R&D using foreign resources, and international standards participation, with Article 72 of the Foreign Trade Law carrying a RMB 50,000 ceiling for an unregistered free-technology contract against the heavier penalties for unlicensed restricted-technology export. Ten days later, at Wuzhen, the three labs that use that route most — DeepSeek, Alibaba's Qwen and MiniMax — described the regime they are about to be governed by: Liu Dayiheng named non-recallability and the absence of an external perimeter; Gao Xi said his colleagues were researching model tiering; Wang Jian said the premise of openness is trustworthiness, controllability and governability. The 2026-11-03 NDRC briefing, reported by Bloomberg, described lifecycle safety standards with incident disclosure and a transition period. Read together, four artefacts from four institutions in three weeks describe a governance regime assembled out of obligations the releasing firm can assert about itself — where the public good is a security commons that no ministry has been funded to operate.
